As someone who has played practically all Ace combat games from Air combat to Ace combat 7 (+ Project Wingman), Ace Combat 8 is probably my favorite Ace Combat right now.

I love how this game serves as a bridge to connect AC7 and AC3, not only thematically like the presence of General Resources but also certain technologies like megafloats or airfighters such as the FA-36. Project Aces absolutely nailed it with AC8 and I'm really proud to say that it's is my GOTY of 2026 but now I'm wondering what's their next step for the franchise. It's clear that we are getting dangerously close to Electrosphere and that's the elephant in the room right now.

Assuming they want to push the narrative further I believe the correct choice would be a remake of Ace Combat 3 with a heavy rework on the missions before making an Ace Combat 9 as a direct sequel. I really wish we can go back to the corporate wars because It has such a perfect worldbuilding, like come on who doesn't want to fly the delphinus Mk.3 (Please Project Aces add it to AC8)

The game positions itself as the absolute pinnacle of the franchise so far, even though the launch has been marred by questionable QoL decisions and some dubious initiatives. This is mainly due to the fact that Ace Combat Zero is treated as a DLC on PC (because it requires the base game to be installed) whereas console players received access to it as a completely standalone title.

On the other side, the game masterfully combines the distinct elements that made past entries so highly praised, uniting them all into a single, cohesive package. While it is still too early for a definitive verdict, it is undeniably on track to become the greatest Ace Combat in history.

Great! It understands what made 7 awesome and doubled down on it. Everything has improved. I liked the plot and characters, and as usual appreciated the vibe/feel and generally emotional run it provides. Great music too. Ace combat keeps being true to itself, a playable anime, on the arcade side. 

As a side note, I do feel the inspiration taken from 7, also in the plot and putting the character at the center, even in some missions. Not necessarily bad, but I would appreciate an evolution next time, this works well since the previous entry was launched a long time ago. 

As for stuff to improve, I would like to have a FOV slider and control of what to disable and what not in the HUD, to allow for a more immersive mode. I would also like to have the key UI baked into the cockpit, and even the helmet as the more modern ones do. It would still be the same game, but play very differently, which in my opinion would be awesome. As a reference, take the metro series.

All in all, another great entry, looking forward to updates, if any.

I came for the fighter jets. I stayed because Ace Combat 8 somehow made me care about the people inside them.

The controls are tight, the visuals are fantastic, and the missions keep finding new ways to raise the stakes. Most of the time, that escalation works beautifully. Once in a while, a mission keeps going past its best moment, or my carefully chosen loadout turns out to be completely wrong for the job. Apparently the enemy got the briefing I missed.

It took me nearly 23 hours to finish, and by the end I was more emotionally invested than I expected from a game about fighter jets and explosions. The music knows exactly when to show up, and the campaign delivers memorable moments without needing to explain them twice. I finished it thinking about the characters, the music, and the ride the game had taken me on.

Technical stuff.
I've seen a lot of negative reviews abot performance of the game and I can't agree with most of them.
So, here is a Linux Gaming(tm) current performance evaluation from me:
tl;dr: **It works great!**
Run immedieately out of the box with default compatability layer.
There was a GPU driver pop-up on startup, prompting to download older version of a driver, but I just dismissed it and haven't experienced any issues. I've let game to handle choice of settings (picked all High); disabled motion blur, capped game to 85FPS and switched to AMD FSR.
According to telemetry GPU haven't hit 100% once and 85 actual FPS by Steam fps counter was steady, with 1% lows to 60 fps.
So, yeah, it works great!
